def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary.title: Operational model, data, calibration and uncertainty vocabulary of the experiment interface
def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR12 reservation ("def operational model/data/calibration/uncertainty vocabulary"); prose-scaffold.md SR12 row ("All four secondary narratives, exact report destinations above; no primary experiment source")
def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary.design_state: explicit-definition-contract; formulation vocabulary only, no measurement, no sampling law and no statistical inference
def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary.physical_scope: Formulation vocabulary inside the flat special-relativity framework: it names run descriptions, operational models, data records, calibration declarations and uncertainty bounds built from the framework's own objects (events, worldlines, clocks, observers, ideal waves, radar readings, observer energies and frequencies) and its SI conventions. It asserts no measurement, no apparatus behaviour, no realized experiment, no sampling law, no statistical inference and no value of any physical constant; in particular it does not claim that any laboratory realizes an operational model.
def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary.statement:
Adopt the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], the ideal-clock and ideal-light assumptions of [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]], the ideal plane-wave and frequency-reading model of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]], the operational radar protocol of [[def-sr-operational-radar-protocol]], the massive-particle measurement identification of [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] clause (ii) and the massless-particle measurement identification of [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]] clause (ii). This definition introduces the framework's experimental-interface vocabulary; it selects no experiment, records no value and asserts no comparison.

**(a) Run descriptions.** A *run description* is a finite tuple $D=(d_1,\dots,d_r)$ whose entries are framework objects of the following kinds, each declared with its domain and regularity as specified by the cited item, together with the frame, observer, event or unit convention required for a numerical reading where such a reading is used: a point of the affine Minkowski space $A$ (an event, [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]); a vector of $V$ of declared causal character ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]); a future timelike worldline together with its proper-time function ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]], [[def-sr-proper-time]]); a future unit timelike vector or a smooth observer congruence ([[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]]); a future null wave covector with its affine phase ([[def-sr-affine-phase-and-wave-covector]]); a radar time or radar distance assigned by the operational radar protocol ([[def-sr-operational-radar-protocol]]); an observer angular frequency ([[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]]); an observer energy, spatial momentum, kinetic energy or invariant mass ([[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]); and a real parameter vector in a declared subset of $\mathbb R^m$ with declared units. A run description is a description of a model configuration; the tuple asserts nothing about any apparatus or about nature.

**(b) Operational model.** An *operational model* is a tuple $M=(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ in which: $S$ is a nonempty set, the *preparation index set*; $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ is a nonempty *parameter set* and $\theta:S\to\Theta$ is a surjection, the *parameter map*; $D$ assigns to each $s\in S$ a run description $D(s)$ of (a); and for some integer $d\ge1$ the map $F:\Theta\to\mathbb R^d$ is a *prediction map* for $D$, subject to the declared interpretation $(*)$: for every $s\in S$, each component of $F(\theta(s))$ is a number that the framework's definitions, postulates and proved consequences assign to the description $D(s)$, with every intermediate quantity, frame, event, sign and unit declared. A pair $(M,F)$ is called an operational model for the quantity whose values $F$ computes. Condition $(*)$ is a declared interpretation that reviewers check when the model is used; it is not a consequence of the tuple structure, and no clause of this definition asserts that any apparatus realizes $M$ or that $F(\theta(s))$ is measured.

**(c) Data records.** A *data record* is a tuple $R=(N,z,\varepsilon,a)$ with an integer $N\ge1$; $z=(z_1,\dots,z_N)$ with $z_k\in\mathbb R^d$; $\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_N)$ with $\varepsilon_k\in[0,\infty)^d$; and $a=(a_1,\dots,a_N)$ a finite tuple of *condition annotations*, each a finite string identifying the declared run condition of the datum and, when the datum is taken from a report, the bibliographic identification of that report. The record declares: for each $k$, the value of the quantity of (b) under the condition annotated by $a_k$ lies in the closed box $\prod_{j=1}^d[z_{k,j}-\varepsilon_{k,j},\,z_{k,j}+\varepsilon_{k,j}]$, in the declared units. A data record contains no probability space, random variable, distribution, sampling law, independence assumption, likelihood or coverage statement; it declares nothing about how the values $z_k$ were produced and nothing about the correctness of any calibration.

**(d) Calibration declarations.** Let $Z$ be a nonempty set of declared *instrument-output values*. A *calibration declaration* is a tuple $C=(Z,c,\delta,h)$ with $c:Z\to\mathbb R^d$, $\delta:Z\to[0,\infty)^d$ and $h$ a condition annotation; it declares that for every $z\in Z$ obtained under the condition annotated by $h$, the value of the declared quantity lies in the closed box $\prod_j[c_j(z)-\delta_j(z),\,c_j(z)+\delta_j(z)]$ in the declared units. A *calibration record* is a data record of (c) whose declared quantity is the value of the calibration map's output. The declaration asserts no accuracy beyond the bound $\delta$ and no statistical property of $c$ or $\delta$.

**(e) Uncertainty vocabulary.** For a data record of (c), the *declared uncertainty* of the $k$-th datum is the vector $\varepsilon_k$; a *source label* is an element of the finite declared set $\{\text{calibration},\ \text{systematic},\ \text{sampling-variability},\ \text{rounding},\ \text{other}\}$ attached to a bound; and a *total declared bound* for a value computed from finitely many recorded values by a declared finite arithmetic expression is any $B\in[0,\infty)$ for which the declaration states: whenever each recorded value lies in its declared closed box, the computed value lies in $[\hat y-B,\hat y+B]$ for the declared number $\hat y$ (for instance, for a sum of recorded scalars the sum of the recorded bounds is such a bound). Every uncertainty entry is a declared constraint of the form in (c) and (d); no probability law, coverage probability, confidence level, p-value or posterior is defined by this vocabulary.

**(f) Comparison claims are separate.** A claim that a data record $R$ and an operational model $M$ are consistent, or that $R$ supports, refutes or fails to distinguish $M$, is not part of (a)-(e): such a claim requires its own statement, a declared comparison rule and its own prerequisites, in particular the primary-report and analysis layer reserved by the source design under the label M20 and not supplied here. No clause of this vocabulary licenses any conclusion about the truth of a postulate or of the framework.

**(g) Well-definedness and scope.** All components of (a)-(e) are finite tuples of sets, maps and real numbers with declared domains and units; the constructions use no choice principle and no measurability, integrability, completeness or differentiability beyond the cited items, and clause (b) evaluates a prediction only at parameter values for which the cited items supply its ingredients. The vocabulary asserts no measurement, no apparatus behaviour, no empirical support or refutation, no value of the constant $c$ or of any other physical parameter, and no statistical inference.
def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary.strategy: A definition item. Well-definedness: (a) enumerates object kinds each supplied by a cited item with its own domain and regularity, and requires the reading conventions to be declared rather than inferred; (b) is a tuple of a set, a subset of $\mathbb R^m$, two maps and a finite tuple, all of them finite data with declared domains; the map $F$ is evaluated only at the parameter values $\theta(s)$ for which the cited items define its ingredients; (c) and (d) are finite tuples of real vectors, nonnegative bounds and annotation strings, so each closed box $\prod_j[z_j-\varepsilon_j,z_j+\varepsilon_j]$ is a well-defined subset of $\mathbb R^d$ because $\varepsilon_j\ge0$; (e) defines the declared-bound vocabulary by a stated property rather than by an extremal or optimality claim, and (f) states the separateness of comparison claims. Condition $(*)$ of (b) is deliberately an interpretation obligation: the definition names the tuple and its intended reading, and any use of an operational model must check $(*)$ against the specific framework items (for the Doppler instance of this page, [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]] supplies it). No choice principle is used anywhere: all constructions are finite tuples and pointwise evaluations. The scope clauses exclude measurements, apparatus behaviour, calibration correctness and all statistical notions; the reader should note that an operational model is a mathematical structure of the framework and not a claim that any laboratory realizes it.

rem-sr-primary-report-research-queue.title: Primary-report research queue for the special-relativity framework
rem-sr-primary-report-research-queue.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR12 reservation ("rem proposed primary-report research queue; no exp item until actual reports read") and its 'Bridges and empirical boundary' section; prose-scaffold.md SR12 row
rem-sr-primary-report-research-queue.design_state: scope-and-queue remark; records declared report destinations, authoring requirements and empirical qualifications; no measurement asserted
rem-sr-primary-report-research-queue.physical_scope: Scope declaration of the framework's empirical interface: it records a research queue of primary-report destinations and the qualifications future experiment items must carry. It asserts no measurement, no dataset, no uncertainty value, no comparison result, no deviation, no empirical support for any postulate and no precision of any physical constant.
rem-sr-primary-report-research-queue.statement:
Scope-and-queue record for the empirical layer of the flat special-relativity framework, stated in the vocabulary of [[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]].

(i) No primary report has been read in the construction of this page; this page records no experiment item, no dataset, no measured value, no calibration, no uncertainty value and no statistical analysis.

(ii) The source design declares four *primary-report search destinations* for future experiment items of this framework. Each is named here as a destination, that is, a family of published reports to retrieve and read in full text, and none of them is evidence for any postulate: (a) historical ether and light-propagation experiments (interferometric or resonance tests of the constancy of the coordinate speed of light between inertial charts, and Doppler-shift tests of moving emitters); (b) unstable-particle lifetime measurements (beam or storage-ring measurements of a particle's lifetime at a measured speed compared with its lifetime at rest); (c) accelerator kinematics of charged particles at high Lorentz factor (measurements of momentum, energy or speed relating a particle's measured quantities to its velocity); (d) clock-transport and clock-comparison experiments (aircraft-, satellite- or laboratory-borne atomic clocks comparing the elapsed times of differently moving or differently situated ideal clocks). The secondary narratives consulted for this page mention instances of these families, among them the historical ether-and-Maxwell context (Crowell pp. 13-15), the 1938 Ives-Stilwell Doppler test (Crowell p. 57), storage-ring muon-lifetime measurements (Crowell pp. 28-29), the 1971 Hafele-Keating aircraft atomic-clock comparison (Crowell pp. 15, 26, 28; Tong pp. 24-25) and a 2010 low-speed atomic-clock measurement (Crowell p. 28); those mentions are contextual motivation only and are not documentation of reported measurements here.

(iii) Before any experiment item can be authored on a destination, the actual primary report must be retrieved and read, and the record must carry the apparatus and preparation, operational definitions of the measured quantities, the calibration model, the sampling and error model, the treatment of systematic errors, the measured values with their reported uncertainties, and the source's limitations. Textbook and review narratives are not substitutes for the primary reports.

(iv) The comparison of model predictions with recorded data is a separate promised physics-theorem obligation which the source design declares to require the primary-report and analysis layer (research label M20); that layer is not supplied, so no experiment item is authored and no comparison is stated until actual reports are read.

(v) Qualifications any future comparison must carry: observations test the combined model and apparatus assumptions; finite-sample agreement does not establish a postulate or a model; a p-value would not be the probability that a theory is false and a confidence level would not be a posterior probability; and a finite bounded record does not by itself determine a unique parameter or adjudicate between distinct models.

(vi) This remark asserts no measurement, no deviation from any model, no empirical support for or against any postulate, and no value, precision or uncertainty of any physical constant.
rem-sr-primary-report-research-queue.strategy: A scope-and-queue remark; its clauses record the design's declared destinations, the authoring requirements for future experiment items and the qualifications such items must carry, and they assert no measurement and no empirical result. (ii) names each destination as a family of reports; the instances in the second sentence are identified as textbook narratives only, following the content model's rule that textbook experiment descriptions are contextual motivation rather than reported observations. (iii) lists the apparatus, preparation, operational-definition, calibration, sampling, systematics, measured-value and limitation fields that any future experiment item must supply; this list is the vocabulary of clause (c) of [[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]] applied to a report. (iv) records the design's M20 dependency for the comparison theorem and its consequence, made concrete by the escalated [[pthm-sr-specified-model-comparison]]. (v) restates the statistical-evidence qualifications that travel with any future comparison; none of them is used as a premise elsewhere. (vi) records the scope of the remark. No proof obligation arises, and no clause asserts the truth of any report or model.

pthm-sr-specified-model-comparison.physical_scope: No physical claim is made by this item in its escalated state: it records that the comparison claim reserved by the source design cannot be formulated or proved without actual primary reports and the analysis layer M20. It asserts no measured value, no dataset, no comparison rule, no model agreement or disagreement, and no empirical support or refutation of any postulate.
pthm-sr-specified-model-comparison.statement:
ESCALATED - no mathematical statement is supplied for this item in this build.

The source design reserves a comparison physics theorem that compares specified model predictions of the special-relativity framework with recorded data, and records that it requires M20, the primary-report and analysis prerequisite. The closure ledger's entry M20 has status "no-experiment-authored; primary-report-queue-retained": no reported primary measurement or experiment item exists, and authoring the analysis requires actual primary reports. The design further directs that no experiment item is authored until actual reports are read. Consequently no dataset, no uncertainty record, no comparison rule and no analysis layer exist against which a comparison theorem could be stated; substituting a textbook narrative, an unread report or invented data for the missing empirical premises would violate the statistical-evidence rules of ../PHYSICS-CONTENT-MODEL.md, and no conditional statement can be recovered from the tuple vocabulary alone because clause (f) of [[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]] makes comparison claims separate and requires their own rule and prerequisites.

This item therefore records the exact obligation and its gap rather than a mathematical claim. A future statement must identify the retrieved primary report or reports, the apparatus and preparation model, the operational definition of each measured quantity, the calibration and sampling models, the exact comparison rule and its error analysis, the physical scope and the inherited uncertainties; its proof would then be a conditional deduction from those qualified empirical premises together with the framework's model predictions, and the conclusion would carry their qualifications. No such premises exist in this run.
pthm-sr-specified-model-comparison.strategy: No proof strategy is recorded: the item is escalated, not ready, and asserts no mathematical claim. Resolution requires one of: (i) the owner authorizing and supplying actual primary reports together with the analysis machinery M20 (or an equivalent complete mathematical analysis layer), after which the theorem can be stated and proved conditionally on the qualified empirical premises and its statement, hypotheses and dependency roles can be scaffolded; or (ii) an owner decision that the comparison theorem is deferred out of this pair's build scope, with a recorded destination. No partial argument, approximation, substitute dataset or fabricated precision is asserted; the examined dependency is [[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]] (scaffolded, ready on this batch), and the missing prerequisite is the M20 primary-report/analysis layer.

ex-sr-operational-record-arithmetic-work.title: Worked instance of the operational vocabulary: an illustrative bounded record for the longitudinal Doppler ratio and its parameter window
ex-sr-operational-record-arithmetic-work.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR12 reservation ("def operational model/data/calibration/uncertainty vocabulary"); B-page construction corresponding to def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary
ex-sr-operational-record-arithmetic-work.design_state: complete elementary worked instance of the vocabulary clauses with exact rational arithmetic; declared illustrative values, not a measurement
ex-sr-operational-record-arithmetic-work.physical_scope: Worked arithmetic instance inside the flat special-relativity framework: it instantiates the operational vocabulary on the framework's own longitudinal Doppler prediction with a declared, explicitly illustrative record. It asserts no apparatus, no measurement, no calibration correctness, no sampling model, no statistical inference and no empirical support or refutation of the Doppler theorem or of any postulate.
ex-sr-operational-record-arithmetic-work.statement:
Adopt the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], the vocabulary of [[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]] and the ideal plane-wave model of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]]. Consider the longitudinal configuration of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]]: inertial charts $x$ and $x'$ whose transition is $x'=B(\beta e_1)\,x$ for a real $\beta\in(-1,1)$, where $B(\cdot)$ is the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]], so that the frame $x'$ moves with velocity $c\beta e_1$ relative to $x$; an ideal emitter at rest in $x$; an ideal plane wave whose frame-$x$ data are $(\omega,s)$ with angular frequency $\omega>0$ and $s=e_1$; and the rest observer of $x'$. By clause (ii) of that theorem this observer reads $\omega_o(\beta)=\gamma_\beta(1-\beta)\omega$ with $\gamma_\beta=(1-\beta^2)^{-1/2}$, so the *Doppler ratio* is $$F(\beta):=\frac{\omega_o(\beta)}{\omega}=\sqrt{\frac{1-\beta}{1+\beta}},\qquad \beta\in(-1,1),$$ the rational power being that of [[def-rational-power]].

(a) Let $S:=\Theta:=(-1,1)$, $\theta:=\mathrm{id}$, let $D(\beta)$ be the run description comprising the inertial charts $x$ and $x'$, the emitter's straight rest worldline in $x$, the future null wave covector with frame-$x$ data $(\omega,e_1)$ and the observer's straight rest worldline in $x'$, and let $F$ be as displayed. Then $M:=(S,\Theta,\theta,D,F)$ is an operational model for the dimensionless ratio $\omega_o/\omega$ in the sense of clause (b) of [[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]]: condition $(*)$ holds with the prediction supplied by the cited Doppler theorem, and $d=1$. The map $F$ is strictly decreasing on $(-1,1)$, and for every real $r>0$ there is exactly one $\beta\in(-1,1)$ with $F(\beta)=r$, namely $$\beta(r)=\frac{1-r^2}{1+r^2};$$ consequently $F$ is a strictly decreasing bijection of $(-1,1)$ onto $(0,\infty)$.

(b) Let $z\in(0,1]$ and $\varepsilon\in[0,z)$ be real, so that $0<z-\varepsilon<z+\varepsilon$, and let $R$ be the declared one-point record with $N=1$, $z_1=z$, $\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon$ and condition annotation 'longitudinal Doppler ratio of the moving observer in the propagation direction' in the sense of clause (c) of the vocabulary. Then the set of parameters consistent with $R$ and $M$, $$C(R,M):=\{\beta\in(-1,1):F(\beta)\in[z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon]\},$$ equals the closed interval $[\beta(z+\varepsilon),\beta(z-\varepsilon)]$; it is nonempty, and every element of it satisfies the declared bound of $R$.

(c) Illustrative instance (declared illustrative values, not a measurement report): $z=9/10$ and $\varepsilon=1/100$. Then $$\beta(91/100)=\frac{1719}{18281}\approx0.094032,\qquad \beta(89/100)=\frac{2079}{17921}\approx0.116009,$$ and $C(R,M)=[1719/18281,\ 2079/17921]$, an interval of exact length $7200000/327613801$ in $\beta$, whose endpoints satisfy $F(1719/18281)=91/100$ and $F(2079/17921)=89/100$.

(d) Scope. Every number in (c) is a declared illustrative value supplied to instantiate the vocabulary's clauses and their arithmetic; the example asserts no apparatus, no calibration correctness, no measurement, no sampling model, no statistical inference and no empirical support or refutation of the Doppler theorem or of any postulate.
ex-sr-operational-record-arithmetic-work.strategy: Direct verification of each clause. (a) Condition $(*)$: the ratio $\omega_o/\omega$ for the fixed configuration $(\beta e_1,\ s=e_1)$ is read by the rest observer of $x'$ as $\gamma_\beta(1-\beta)$ by clause (ii) of [[pthm-sr-null-wave-doppler-and-aberration]] with $\beta\cdot s=\beta$ and $|\beta|<1$; since $1-\beta>0$ and $1+\beta>0$ for $\beta\in(-1,1)$, the identity $\gamma_\beta(1-\beta)=\sqrt{(1-\beta)/(1+\beta)}$ is an elementary consequence of the rational-power laws [[lem-rational-power-laws]] and of the positivity of the square root, with the sign chosen positive. Strict decrease: for $-1<\beta_1<\beta_2<1$, the inequality $(1-\beta_1)/(1+\beta_1)>(1-\beta_2)/(1+\beta_2)$ is equivalent, after multiplying by the positive product $(1+\beta_1)(1+\beta_2)$ ([[lem-of-sign-rules]]), to $2(\beta_1-\beta_2)<0$, which holds; composing with the strictly increasing square-root map ([[lem-rational-power-monotone]], claim 2 with $r=1/2$) gives $F(\beta_1)>F(\beta_2)$. The inverse: $F(\beta)=r$ for $r>0$ is equivalent to $(1-\beta)/(1+\beta)=r^2$, that is to $\beta(1+r^2)=1-r^2$, i.e. $\beta=\beta(r)$; this $\beta(r)$ lies in $(-1,1)$ because $|1-r^2|<1+r^2$, and the solution is unique by strict monotonicity. (b) Since $F$ is strictly decreasing with inverse $\beta(\cdot)$, $F(\beta)\in[z-\varepsilon,z+\varepsilon]$ is equivalent to $\beta\in[\beta(z+\varepsilon),\beta(z-\varepsilon)]$, and both endpoints lie in $(-1,1)$ because $z-\varepsilon>0$ makes $z+\varepsilon>0$; the declared box of the record is a closed interval in the value variable. (c) Substitute $r=91/100$ and $r=89/100$ into $\beta(r)$ and reduce: exact rational arithmetic; the length is $\beta(89/100)-\beta(91/100)$, computed by common denominators as $7200000/327613801>0$. The decimals are displayed to six places and are not used in any claim. No step uses a probability model, a sampling assumption or a measurement.

cex-sr-bounded-record-does-not-identify-.title: Counterexample: a bounded one-point record need not determine the parameter of an operational model
cex-sr-bounded-record-does-not-identify-.reference: content-model statistical-evidence guidance ("a finite sample can lack ...", "a bounded record does not determine a unique parameter"); B-page construction corresponding to def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary
cex-sr-bounded-record-does-not-identify-.design_state: complete refutation by two exact rational parameter witnesses consistent with one illustrative bounded record; declared illustrative values
cex-sr-bounded-record-does-not-identify-.physical_scope: Conceptual counterexample inside the flat special-relativity framework: it shows that a declared bounded record of the operational vocabulary need not determine a unique parameter of an operational model, using the framework's own Doppler prediction and declared illustrative values. It asserts no measurement, no statistical inference and no empirical conclusion about any model or postulate.
cex-sr-bounded-record-does-not-identify-.statement:
**Statement refuted.** A declared one-point data record of the vocabulary with positive declared uncertainty determines the parameter of an operational model uniquely: if a record $R$ of clause (c) of [[def-sr-experiment-interface-vocabulary]] is consistent with two parameters $\beta_1,\beta_2$ of one operational model $M$, then $\beta_1=\beta_2$.

**Counterexample.** Take $M$ and $R$ as in [[ex-sr-operational-record-arithmetic-worked]] with the illustrative record $z=9/10$, $\varepsilon=1/100$, so that $M$ is the longitudinal Doppler operational model of that example and $$F(\beta)=\sqrt{\frac{1-\beta}{1+\beta}},\qquad C(R,M)=[1719/18281,\ 2079/17921].$$ Put $\beta_1:=1719/18281$ and $\beta_2:=2079/17921$. Both lie in $(-1,1)$, and clause (c) of that example gives $F(\beta_1)=91/100$ and $F(\beta_2)=89/100$, so both values lie in the record's declared interval $[89/100,91/100]$; hence $R$ is consistent with $\beta_1$ and with $\beta_2$. The two parameters are distinct: $$\beta_2-\beta_1=\frac{2079}{17921}-\frac{1719}{18281}=\frac{7200000}{327613801}>0,$$ the numerator and denominator being positive integers (denominator $17921\cdot18281=327613801$). Therefore the refuted statement is false. In fact $R$ is consistent with every parameter in the whole interval $[1719/18281,\ 2079/17921]$, so this bounded record does not determine the parameter even up to the endpoints of a positive-length interval; and nothing in the consistency of $R$ with $M$ supports the truth of $M$ or of any postulate. The numerical values are declared illustrative values, not a measurement report.
cex-sr-bounded-record-does-not-identify-.strategy: Refutation by explicit witnesses, using the earlier example on this page. By clause (b) of [[ex-sr-operational-record-arithmetic-worked]] the consistency set of the record is the interval $[\beta(z+\varepsilon),\beta(z-\varepsilon)]=[1719/18281,2079/17921]$, and clause (c) evaluates $F$ at both endpoints as $91/100$ and $89/100$, which lie in the declared interval $[89/100,91/100]$; a parameter is consistent exactly when its $F$-value lies in that interval, so both endpoints are consistent with $R$. Distinctness is the exact rational difference computed in the statement: cross-multiplying, $2079\cdot18281-1719\cdot17921=38006199-30806199=7200000>0$ over the positive product denominator, so $\beta_2>\beta_1$; the arithmetic is exact rational arithmetic in the ordered field $\mathbb R$. This contradicts the refuted uniqueness claim. Nothing in the construction uses or asserts a probability model, a measurement or a calibration; the illustrative values are declared as such.
